evals.prompt: I have a coherent LunaTalk card draft, but the public-facing package is weak: roleName is generic, roleDesc is too long, tags are vague, and a new player cannot tell why to open it. I do not want MCP calls yet.
evals.expected_output: Routes to lunatalk-profile-packager, preserves the existing engine, returns a profile package packet with roleName candidates, roleDesc candidates, a specific tag set, first-impression check, and no MCP calls.
expectations: The output treats the issue as profile packaging / promise compression, not publish readiness or whole-card rewriting.
The output produces three roleName candidates with different promise angles.
The output produces roleDesc candidates that include player relation, tension, and play loop while staying scannable.
The tag set uses concrete card shape, relationship or role axis, action loop, tone/rating, and mechanic/format signals.
The output does not call MCP tools, render, simulate, publish, or claim platform performance.

evals.prompt: Make this already-planned zh-Hant daily-life neighbor card easier to understand from the card profile. The routine engine and opening are done; I only need roleName, a short roleDesc, and tags before field assembly.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the daily-life engine intact, packages the profile in zh-Hant, avoids re-blueprinting, and hands off to draft-only card authoring after the profile package packet.
expectations: The output preserves the existing daily-life packet or engine instead of reopening premise workshop.
The roleDesc pattern promises routine, player relation, small pressure, and play loop in Traditional Chinese.
The tags include daily-life or slice-of-life, relationship/role axis, action loop, and tone without vague duplicates.
The first-impression check verifies that the first screen can prove the public promise.
The output hands off to lunatalk-card-author only after the profile package is coherent.

evals.prompt: My RPG card has a solid play-engine packet, but the roleDesc reads like a manual and the tags are just fantasy, adventure, magic. Compress the public promise without cutting the rules.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-profile-packager with play-engine preservation, moves manual details out of roleDesc, creates RPG/system tags tied to player controls/resources/risk, and routes token or authoring only if needed.
expectations: The output preserves the play-engine packet and does not delete resources, state, or turn protocol from the engine.
The roleDesc candidates summarize player position, system/world, resource or risk pressure, and state/route change.
The output cuts manual detail from roleDesc and keeps durable rules in roleDetailDesc.
The tags include primary shape, action loop, and mechanic signals rather than only broad fantasy mood.
The output avoids MCP calls and unsupported popularity/ranking claims.

evals.prompt: I want a title and tagline for a card idea, but the premise is still only 'cozy vampire maybe mystery maybe romance'. I need the public package.
evals.expected_output: Routes away from profile packaging because the premise is not settled, asks for or requires premise workshop first, and does not invent final roleName/roleDesc/tags.
expectations: The output recognizes that profile packaging requires a chosen premise or engine.
The output routes to lunatalk-premise-workshop before final profile fields.
The output may suggest packaging criteria but does not lock final roleName, roleDesc, or tags.
The output does not call MCP tools.
The output keeps popular/top-card language as public craft goals if mentioned.

evals.prompt: Package this coherent card profile so it sounds top-tier and more popular than nearby cards. The engine is done, but roleName and roleDesc are bland. Do not use MCP tools.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-profile-packager, translates top-tier/popular language into public craft goals, avoids ranking/source/traffic claims, preserves the engine, and returns profile candidates without MCP calls.
expectations: The output treats popular/top-tier language as craft goals such as clarity, specificity, agency, hook, and honest first-screen proof.
The output does not claim platform ranking, traffic, source-card analysis, private-example access, or non-public performance knowledge.
The output does not replace unsupported popularity claims with market words like premium, high-demand, viral, trending, best, or top-ranked.
The output preserves the existing card engine and patches only roleName, roleDesc, tags, and first-impression promise.
The output returns roleName candidates, roleDesc candidates, tag set, first-impression check, and handoff.
The output does not call MCP tools, render, simulate, publish, or add server gates.
